newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end higher after strong retail sales.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end higher after strong retail sales.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 93.10 (PREV 93.21) 90-DAYS 6.95 (PREV 6.86)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.50 PCT (PREV 6.50) US 5-YR 6.27 (PREV 6.34)
NZ MCI -0.85 (PREV -0.90)
* Bill futures drop 12 points on profit taking, stop losses
* Retail sales rise 7.9 pct in April, trend still flat
* Selloff not seen sustained, economy still weak
New Zealand yields closed higher across the curve on Tuesday with the short end taking a moderately heavy bath.
September bill futures fell 12 basis points to 93.10 on steady volume of 3810.

Selling was across the curve. While the trend may continue on Wednesday, dealers said weakness in the economy, despite the 7.9 percent rise in April retail sales, ought to put a floor under the market.
A bill trader said a long market felt heavy before the retail sales number and that provided a good excuse to unload.
Profit takers took out some stop losses.
"Now that its broken through 93.20 it's not looking too good," he said.
The 90-day bills were likely to have a test of 7.00 percent again but that level is seen as good buying.
The bond market, after opening up with a firm tone, quickly ran into supply, particularly in the longer bonds.
Domestic selling predominated.
One bank chief dealer said the strong retail sales in April merely corrected weak data in the last couple of months.
"I think the market is still in reasonably good shape. We have just seen some weak longs exiting the market in the last day or so and that may continue.

"But once the fog clears, people will realise the economy is still not in great shape. It hasn't changed our view on a likely easing at the end of the month. The market will see sense reasonably quickly and I don't think this will be a sustained sell-off."
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington Newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
